description.narrative: Stöd till ECPAT International som verkar globalt för att skydda barn mot sexuellt våld och exploatering.
Support to ECPAT International, a network of organisations that work for childrens rights and child protection.

The vision of ECPAT is a world where all children enjoy their fundamental rights free from sexual exploitation. Their mission is to push for the critical systemic and social changes necessary to end the sexual exploitation of children (SEC) in partnership with governments, intergovernmental institutions, the private sector, civil society, and the public, including children themselves.
The strategic framework objectives for the network are:
For systematic change (strategic goal 1) - Increased adoption and implementation of comprehensive legal, policy and regulatory frameworks for addressing SEC including its new forms (online): ECPAT will analyze national legal frameworks on SEC and promote correct terminology in laws, policies and media; improve the capacity of legal professionals and engage citizens in demanding better laws and policies.
- Increased capacity of law enforcement, courts and accompanying lawyers for the investigation, prosecution, and prevention of SEC: ECPAT will research effective systems and responses for law enforcement and promote what works; and facilitate multi-country collaboration, especially between countries of origin of perpetration and countries were children experience exploitation.
- Increased private sector regulation, financial commitment, and action for child protection: ECPAT will promote the implementation of codes of conduct for self -regulation as well as for meeting mandates by governments and regulatory bodies; build the capacity of relevant sectors to prevent and respond; and build the capacity of the media to use appropriate terminology
- Increased access to quality, child-friendly and effective protection, response and support systems and services for at-risk children and children who have experienced the sexual exploitation of children: ECPAT will conduct innovative research, amplify existing research, and on the ground successes to inform training programs and child safeguarding standards for welfare and front-line staff; manage evidence based model programs to be handed over to national governments. People who experienced sexual exploitation when they were children will be consulted to help define response and support services.
For social change (strategic goal 2) - Greater awareness, help-seeking and freedom from stigma and shame around the sexual exploitation of children among children, survivors, caregivers, and vulnerable communities, through use of preventative education and public information: ECPAT will advocate and support the design and implementation of evidence-based education and training for children, caregivers and vulnerable communities, including age-appropriate sex and sexuality education; promote help seeking among children and vulnerable communities and engage with survivors to promote preventative measures. ECPAT will also collaborate with the governments to address the push factors such as economic disparities, address the demand side of SEC by advocating for offender interventions and rehabilitation and promote the establishment of reporting mechanism for victims, such as hotlines and help lines
- Greater public visibility and awareness of the problem, through the collection and promotion of disaggregated and representative data at the national level: ECPAT will design practical research methodologies and measurement tools, support countries to replicate studies and research projects and help facilitate better quality research through ethical guidelines. ECPAT will also engage in existing large scale research initiative to ensure SEC indicator are integrated.
For each of these objectives a number of indicators have been developed. ECPAT will establish a baseline and develop national action plans which reflect both the national context and current priorities.
Specific secretariat objectives have been developed for advocating governments and engage with the private sector, including for financial commitments, promotion of preventative and responsive measures and for collecting disaggregated and representative data about SEC.
These objectives are: - Advocate for increased actions by governments leading to the adoption and implementation of legal and policy frameworks. The secretariat will develop common advocacy and position papers and promote international legal standard. This will build on the knowledge and expertise on SEC within the organization
- Advocate for increased political and financial commitments by governments for strengthened law enforcement and better access to justice systems. The secretariat will tap into ongoing advocacy and campaigns, undertake research into and promote effective systems and responses for law enforcement as well as facilitate multicounty collaboration, especially to address increased vulnerability of children through socio-economic disparities.
- Engage with private sector leading to more concrete actions to improve child protection. The secretariat will advocate for binding human rights standards for targeted sector industries to include childrens right and child protection measures, including in on-line gaming. Codes of conduct will be promoted and implemented (through the Code) in the travel and tourism industries. Both mandates set by governments and self-regulatory bodies will be advocated for.
- Promote increased access to adequate response and support systems for at-risk children and victims of SEC. The secretariat will build technical expertise of the network by collecting on the ground success to inform best practice programs and initiatives and conduct innovative research. They will play a key role in knowledge leadership, facilitation, and coordination.
- Promote and support the use of preventative education initiatives that stop all types of SEC, leading to greater awareness among children and parents and caregivers. The secretariat will advocate for and support the design and implementation of evidence based preventable education and training program children, adults and vulnerable communities.
- Advocate for state responsibility towards regularly collecting and making public, disaggregated and representative data about SEC. The secretariat will design practical research methodologies and measurement tools for understanding the modus of operand of offenders and the changing trends of SEC, and support members to take on and replicating models developed or tested by the secretariat.
The secretariat will also develop Global Progress Indicators, to track the state of SEC against pre-identified parameters. This will enable more effective national and global advocacy and call for better access to quality data.
To meet the overarching strategic goals of systemic and social change, four influencing for change strategies have been developed: - strengthening the networks influencing role and coordination - identify and disseminate evidence based solutions - convene a wide range of stakeholders for effective partnerships - and express a bolder voice to amplify the voices and perspectives of children These strategies also have specific indicators which will help measure the role of the secretariat. A number of assumptions has also been developed by ECPAT (2.1 proposal), as well as a risk register and a risk appetite statement.

The latest results update: The results presented is a summary from ECPAT´s annual report covering the period 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30.
*International assembly and governance review: The ECPAT Board met in person by the end of September 2022 and agreed on a number of roadmaps for its Board Committees covering e.g., human resource policies and procedures, financial systems and procedures, the overall registration status of the organization, as well as governance review and membership policies. Sida will need to ask for continues updates on these work areas.
*Communications: Website enhancements, including better backend integration of the different digital communication channels. Since the upgrade, the ECPAT website hosts on average 10,000 users/month. The Global Progress Indicators (GPI) a visual dynamic tool showing the state of progress or lack of by governments in addressing the sexual exploitation of children, went live on the website during this period. GPI is also an open data tracking tool for monitoring national responses to child sexual exploitation, measured against 9 indicators ranging from laws to response and prevention measures. ECPAT released a series under the podcast titled Ending the Silence on Child Sexual Exploitation. The series focuses on the thematic areas, e.g., Boys, Online/Digital Technology, Travel & Tourism. The podcast helped to increase awareness of the issues and developed in a simpler format to allow for engagement on emerging trends what stakeholders, communities and society can do to provide support. To date, the podcast has been played over 10,000 times (for other online metrics see the annual report, p. 6).
*Resource mobilization: The budget for the current period (July 2022 June 2023) is currently fully secured at a level of USD 4.3M and will likely expand further, allowing for consolidation and further expansion. Engagement with key donors resulted in better funding opportunities and collaboration opportunities for ECPAT. This has already resulted in six new grant approvals. Furthermore, other prospective donors are in various stages of negotiations and discussions with decisions expected to close in the new fiscal period. Increased engagement with members has led to collaborative conversations on fundraising, ranging from fiscal support to capacity building.
*Travel and tourism: The ongoing engagement and advocacy efforts from ECPAT, led to the: ASEAN Tourism Ministers endorsing the postCOVID19 Recovery Plan for ASEAN Tourism with specific recommendations to protect children from sexual exploitation including adhering to the Code of Conduct developed by ECPAT for the private sector. The topic of child protection, especially in the context of tourism recovery and economic revival being included in key forums. The World Travel and Tourism Council (WTTC) a key partner and an influential stakeholder within the travel and tourism sector, provided a global venue at their annual global summit to address child protection as part of sustainable travel and tourism development. The risk assessment tool was developed by ECPAT to help businesses in travel & tourism as well as ICT (communication & technology) industries to assess and understand their potential risks in relation to child sexual exploitation and trafficking and take action to protect children.
*Global boys initiative: During the reporting period, ECPAT published ten national studies on the issue of sexual exploitation of boys, adding important data and information to the Global Literature Review conducted earlier on the issue. The launches of the reports have been supported by targeted media campaign to support their dissemination and to raise awareness on the issue of sexual exploitation of boys amongst professionals and the general public. These activities allowed ECPAT to begin the conversation on the sexual exploitation and abuse of boys and of children with a different sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, and position it as a key child protection issue, requiring precise strategies and global solutions.
*Technology facilitated sexual exploitation of children: ECPAT continued to monitor and comment on EU developments related to online child sexual abuse and exploitation and the protection of children in the digital environment. In coordination with 18 EU based network members and other civil society partners, ECPAT directly engaged with EU policymakers to influence key discourse and debates which would have important impact on the political mechanisms (see p. 14 of annual report for details). ECPAT leads on the coordination of the CSO Reference Group of WePROTECT Global Alliance as part of global advocacy efforts to keep the topic on the agenda of governments ECPAT leading on advocacy initiatives within ASEAN and in partnership with WePROTECT Global Alliance. ASEAN Member States have in a formal regional Declaration committed to further protect children from all forms of online exploitation and abuse by prioritizing seven measures, representing the key elements that can help shape a safer digital world for children in the ASEAN region and beyond. Crucial evidence from research projects Disrupting Harm, Survivors Perspectives were published during the reporting period. Research about child sexual exploitation and abuse online has received increased attention, particularly in the shift to further online presence during the pandemic.
*Research, legal and policy: During the reporting period, six country reports, for Kenya, Uganda, Thailand, Tanzania, Ethiopia, and the Philippines, were finalized and successfully launched under the Disrupting Harm (DH) project, a multicountry research project by ECPAT, INTERPOL, UNICEF Office of Research Innocenti, aimed at exploring online child sexual exploitation and abuse across 13 countries in Asia and Africa. Survivor conversations approach: To address a global gap in the research, ECPAT has developed the Survivor Conversations approach, a carefully designed way of conducting research with survivors of child sexual exploitation and abuse. In early 2022, ECPAT developed and launched two issues papers exploring how voluntourism may facilitate sexual exploitation of children including identifying solutions to address the risks and how extraterritorial jurisdiction and extradition legislation can be used as tools to tackle the sexual exploitation of children. ECPAT also signed its first contract with the Secretariat of the Lanzarote Committee, to be supported by a grant to produce monitoring reports on the state of implementation of the Lanzarote Convention. As part of the ongoing global legal and policy advocacy, ECPAT coordinated a joint network submission (18 ECPAT member organizations) to the Office of the Special Rapporteur on the Sale and Sexual Exploitation of Children to inform the thematic report on a practical approach to addressing the sale and sexual exploitation of children. ECPAT coordinated a joint network submission (16 ECPAT members) to the Office of the Special Rapporteur on the Sale and Sexual Exploitation of Children to inform the thematic report on addressing the vulnerabilities of children to sale and sexual exploitation in the framework of the SDGs.
*Collaboration with the UN Special Representative on Violence AgainstChildren (SRSG): ECPAT has developed an excellent collaboration with the SRSG leading to joint advocacy in support of field missions, as well as the contribution and alignment according to the thematic the annual reports to the Human Right Council and General Assembly. For instance, the ED of ECPAT coChair with the SRSG a working group galvanizing senior engagement to buildup mobilization in anticipation of SRSG report to the General Assembly in September 2023 on child protection in travel and tourism. ECPAT plans to contribute with thematic parallel report and side events in New York in October 2023 with the SRSG to amplify the commitment of various sectors against sexual exploitation of children, including from financial institutions, law enforcement agencies and actors from the informal economic sector. The GIZ confirmed support to a project that will enable children from Ecuador and Costa Rica to evaluate how adults have been dealing with the development of the tourism sector, sharing their perspective in New York to enrich the discussion. The SRSG is the greatest champion of meaningful child participation in the UN system and the critical contribution made by SRSG to many working groups, sectors and countries is critical to movement building and impact in the fight against sexual exploitation of children.
